Through: Mr. Vishal Raj Sehijpa  Suhail Khan, Advocat  versus  STATE OF NCT OF DELHI & ANR. ..
 Through: Mr. Satinder Singh Baw  the State with Insp.
 and SI Vipin Rathi, 
 Bagh  Mr. Kuldeep Kumar an  Gurpreet Kaur, Advoc  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SAURABH BANERJEE  ORDER % 12.12.2023 1.

The petitioners, vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973

, seek quashing of FIR No.22/2022 dated 06.01.2022 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S. Shalimar Bagh, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement Agreement dated 19.09.2023 arrived at between the parties at Mediation Centre, Rohini Courts,
New Delhi.

2. This petition is accompanied by the Settlement Agreement dated 19.09.2023 [Annexure-A-3] and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
3. Petitioner nos.1 to 4 as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.
CRL.M.C. 9097/2023 page 1 of 2
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 14/12/2023 at 02:19:45 5.
Learned APP for the State accepts notice.

He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.

1 6.
Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.
Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 06.11.2023.

She further affirms the Settlement Agreement dated 19.09.2023 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.5,50,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs.2,50,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no. 2 vide Manager's Cheque no.015697 issued on 28.11.2023 [HDFC Bank] in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony,
maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.
